drills.q: 24/7 N2 VM costs $0.10/hr on-demand. Approximate monthly cost with SUD?
drills.a: 730h x $0.10 = $73 full price; full-month SUD nets ~30% off -> ~$51/month. Tiers apply incrementally below 100% usage.

drills.q: Team wants cheapest VMs and picks E2 for a 24/7 baseline. What discount reality check do you run?
drills.a: E2 gets no SUD. Compare E2 list price vs discounted eligible family (N2/N4 at up to ~30% off or CUD-covered). For steady baselines the discounted N-series can close or invert the gap.

drills.q: Design capacity for 40 vCPU steady + 60 vCPU daytime burst + nightly render farm.
drills.a: Steady: resource-based CUD (commit 80-90% of measured baseline) possibly with reservations. Burst: autoscaled on-demand/SUD, or Autopilot pods. Renders: Spot MIGs with checkpointing. Never commit CUDs to burst/spot components.

drills.q: Post-migration Autopilot bill doubled. Give four causes ranked.
drills.a: 1) Inflated pod requests carried from Standard sizing (requests are the bill). 2) Special-hardware pods flipped to per-node billing + premium. 3) DaemonSets/storage requests now billed per pod/node. 4) Regional spread multiplying footprint via zone skew.

drills.q: Render farm on Spot keeps losing work mid-frame. Redesign.
drills.a: Checkpoint partial state to GCS every N minutes; handle the 30-second ACPI notice with a termination handler that drains; size for throughput-after-evictions; prefer smaller tasks so eviction loses less; keep results idempotent.

drills.q: New cluster, team of 5, variable load, one GPU inference service. Mode?
drills.a: Autopilot: variable load favors per-pod billing; GPUs supported via ComputeClass - but note that GPU pod bills per-node+premium, so compare against a small Standard pool with CUD if GPU runs hot 24/7. Default Autopilot unless GPU economics dominate.

drills.q: Standard cluster at 35% utilization. Rank interventions by effort-to-impact.
drills.a: 1) Packing/consolidation + tighter autoscaler scale-down. 2) Move bursty services to Cloud Run/Autopilot keeping steady platform workloads. 3) Migrate remaining variable workloads to Autopilot. 4) Only then right-size families/CUDs. Discounts before discipline just discount waste.

drills.q: Kafka on GKE loses quorum every node upgrade. YAML fixes vs platform answer?
drills.a: YAML: PDB maxUnavailable=1, zonal anti-affinity, regional PDs StatefulSet, maintenance windows. Platform answer: managed messaging or dedicated VMs decouple quorum availability from node churn - shared nodes couple them by construction.

drills.q: When is plain Compute Engine the right choice over both GKE modes?
drills.a: Few long-lived monoliths, node-locked licensed software, workloads whose ops model is one-VM-one-service, or strict requirements (custom kernel, specific OS) Kubernetes adds nothing to. K8s overhead buys nothing there.

drills.q: Why might you NOT buy 3-year CUDs on a service launched 6 months ago?
drills.a: Baseline unproven - resource CUDs bill regardless of usage for 3 years. Commit below measured baseline (~80-90%), consider spend-based flexible commitments, revisit after a year of stable telemetry.
